context.purpose: Publish PNG frames, timed sprite sheets or an exclusive frame range from an existing silent MP4/H.264 or Matroska/FFV1 source. Output fps retimes the selected presentation frames. Optional deliverable requirements constrain dimensions, duration, bytes and per-frame RGB error.
context.assumptions: Exactly one node; explicit input order and constant frame rate. A matching ffprobe executable is required beside FFmpeg. The adaptor uses their public command-line interfaces.
context.constraints: One node, no audio or arbitrary filter graph. Existing-video sources: 1..600 frames, 32 MiB input, 192 MiB RGB, 4096 px per side, integer constant rate; no interlacing, non-square pixels or rotation/stream side data. MP4 edit lists use native presentation semantics. PNG alpha composites black; H.264 is lossy and needs even dimensions.
context.inspection: Inspect video and retained native decode/probe evidence. Verify dimensions, frame count, rate and duration, and every decoded frame. FFV1 must match RGB bytes; H.264 mean RGB error is bounded at 16/255 per frame. These are bounded fidelity checks, not perceptual certification. Deliverable acceptance is independently reconstructed from authored requirements and actual retained native observations.
context.recovery: INVALID_RESOURCE requires absolute PNG/metadata paths. Missing inputs need actual files, not placeholder paths. Correct dimensions or frame timing for native rejection; use FFV1 if H.264 exceeds the fidelity bound. Replan and rerun with retained failure logs. DELIVERABLE_NOT_MET retains a correct video with observed requirements and corrective next actions; revise sources, fps or codec before a fresh run. INVALID_FRAME_RANGE requires a nonempty zero-based inclusive-start/exclusive-end range within the complete source. UNSUPPORTED_VIDEO requires a supported silent progressive source with uniform presentation timestamps.

workflow.scope: Consumes image, spriteSheet, spriteMetadata and bounded MP4/H264 or Matroska/FFV1 video artifacts; fixed output rate, silent publications, no automatic conversion.

composition.scope: Shared document references, pure value functions and expressions resolve for every finite analytic visit before native validation.

lifecycle.timeout: Native encoding and decoding use a shared elapsed-time budget.
lifecycle.cancellation: Owned native subprocess trees use shared cancellation and retain partial evidence.
lifecycle.logs: Retain stage stdout/stderr, commands, probe output, decoded RGB and submissions.
lifecycle.verification: Recheck full decoded RGB against retained inputs, dimensions, count, duration, hashes and declared codec-dependent error limits. Authored deliverable acceptance is reconstructed from native duration, dimensions/count, actual compressed byte size and per-frame mean RGB errors; unmet results cannot be published as successes. New native decode/probe launchers bind the encoded input digest to each owned stage; launcher source, bindings and decoded/probe output digests are replayed offline. Historical direct commands remain explicitly unbound. Source capture and scheduler fingerprints reject non-regular inputs before opening and recheck descriptors, with bounded byte reads. Existing video sources retain every decoded frame plus captured compressed bytes; bound source probe/decode launchers and full-source cadence validation precede pure index slicing. Native source processes have POSIX memory/file caps; all stages share one timeout.

data.scope: Equal dimensions and bounded non-interlaced PNG subset.

losses: Frame duration must be representable at the chosen constant fps.
H.264 is lossy; FFV1 is byte-exact after alpha compositing.

traits.frameIndices: zero-based presentation frames, inclusive start/exclusive end
traits.frameRate: integer constant source rate; output fps retimes selection

losses: FFV1 output preserves source decoded RGB, not pre-compression source colours.
No colour-management guarantee; non-square pixels, rotation/side data and interlacing rejected.
data.scope: Exactly one video stream, <=600 frames,32 MiB compressed,192 MiB RGB; fixed local demuxers; default MP4 edit-list presentation is honoured.

inspection.scope: Inspect retained probe and verification JSON.
inspection.limits: Video playback is external; the shared console does not advertise a video player.

authoring.reuse: Bind a captured source video; select startFrame inclusive/endFrame exclusive and choose output fps to retime. Changes to source bytes invalidate scheduler reuse; replan and run into a fresh directory.

mpi.scope: Only serial execution is qualified; do not request multiple ranks.

reusable-inputs.scope: The registered hook hashes external inputs for scheduler reuse.

time-batches.scope: No finite native time-list batching support in this route.

source-authoring.scope: Edit ordinary JSON through the shared draft source; planning checks the current revision.

property-authoring.scope: Use atomic JSON pointer patches through the shared draft model; node commands apply only to node-shaped routes.

live-editing.scope: Use bounded batch execution; no persistent native editing session is promised.

native-save.scope: Inspect and reuse declared publications; no console native-save extension is advertised for this route.

conversion.scope: Explicit PNG/sprite-sheet or bounded existing-video frame-range conversion to silent H.264/FFV1; FFV1 preserves decoded source RGB, H.264 is lossy. No automatic conversion planning.

cases.scope: One known PNG encoded as FFV1 at 25 fps; independently decoded RGB must be byte-exact after alpha compositing. Does not qualify H.264 or sprite timing.
One known PNG encoded as FFV1 at 12 fps; independently decoded RGB must be byte-exact after alpha compositing. Does not qualify H.264 or sprite timing.

Known 2x2 RGBA PNG encoded as one FFV1 frame at 25 fps: declared dimensions/frame count, 0.04s native duration within 0.001s, file size below 100000 bytes, and exact decoded composited RGB. No perceptual or general encoding qualification.

Known six-frame 32x24 FFV1 source at 10 fps; presentation range yields 3 frames at 12 fps, independently decoded RGB exact. Source capture/selection/readback; does not qualify arbitrary MP4 edits or audio.
